h1: The glow stack (BPC-157, TB-500 and GHK-Cu): no study has tested it, and each component's human evidence used a different route
dek: Three compounds injected together for skin, hair and healing. Each has real human research behind it. The copper peptide's is face cream, the thymosin work is eye drops and infusions, and BPC-157's human record is two people. None of it describes what this stack does.

queries.heading: Which peptide do celebrities use?
queries.answer: Celebrity attribution is not evidence and this page does not trade in it. What can be said is that the copper peptide in this stack has a long cosmetic history in topical form, which is why it appears in skincare products sold openly, and that no celebrity's routine has been published as a study.

information_gain: The only page on this query to check what each component's human evidence actually is, rather than citing that it exists. GHK-Cu's human studies are topical: wrinkle depth and skin quality after creams, satisfaction after laser resurfacing, scalp flaking. The thymosin beta-4 human work is eye drops for dry eye, intravenous pharmacokinetics and a cardiac study, not subcutaneous TB-500. BPC-157's human record in this ledger is two people. So the stack injects three compounds whose human evidence was produced by a cream, a drop and a case description. The only page to state that no study has given the three together, with the single paper naming any of them in combination identified as a review of six peptides. And the only page to separate the plausible part of the rationale, that the three act on different repair mechanisms, from the claim people actually buy, which is a visible cosmetic result.
serp_format_rewarded: An evidence page in a results set that has none. A Reddit thread ranks fourth and the best commercial page carries two citations. Checking the route on each component's human studies is a gap nobody has filled.
